rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ signs are the markers that establish the truth of his prophethood.
rows.anchor: بعلاماتنا التي تدل على صحة نبوته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A clear sultan is a manifest proof; it is called sultan because it is God’s proof on earth.
rows.anchor: والسلطان إنما سمي سلطانا لأنه حجة الله في أرضه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sultan derives from salīt, something used for lighting; oil is therefore also called salīt.
rows.anchor: واشتقاق السلطان من السليط، والسليط ما يضاء به، ومن هذا قيل للزيت سليط.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh’s malāʾ were his leading people, distinguished by judgment and ability.
rows.anchor: ملؤه أشراف قومه، الذين هم ملاء بالرأي والمقدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following Pharaoh’s command means that they preferred blindness to guidance.
rows.anchor: أي استحبوا العمى على الهدى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb yaqdam means to go ahead of a people; Pharaoh leads his people to the Fire, as the next clause confirms.
rows.anchor: يقال قدمت القوم أقدمهم قدما وقدوما إذا تقدمتهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both occurrences of man are nominative through sawāʾ, which requires two parties, as in saying Zayd and ʿAmr are equal.
rows.anchor: رفع بسواء، وكذلك (من) الثانية يرتفعان جميعا بسواء، لأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because sawāʾ is a verbal noun, the following nouns are raised by ellipsis: the sense is ‘possessors of equality’; verbal nouns do not directly raise nouns as participles do.
rows.anchor: لأن سواء مصدر فلا يجوز أن يرتفع ما بعده إلا على الحذف،

rows.speaker: الخنساء
rows.claim: Al-Khansāʾ’s line illustrates the omitted possessive noun: in reality she is possessed of coming and going.
rows.anchor: كما قالت الخنساء: ترتع ما غفلت حتى إذا ادكرت. . . فإنما هي إقبال وإدبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction is so common with sawāʾ that it has come to behave like an active participle.
rows.anchor: وهذا مما كثر استعماله أعني سواء، فجرى مجرى أسماء الفاعلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second analysis treats the nominative as a predicate meaning ‘equal’; Sibawayh considers this poor because indefinite active participles are too weak to begin a clause, treating them like verbs.
rows.anchor: في موضع مستو، إلا أن سيبويه يستقبح ذلك،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse declares that God knows what is hidden and what is witnessed.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الآية إعلامهم أن الله عز وجل يعلم ما غاب عنهم وما شهد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mustakhfin by night means concealed, since night conceals more than day.
rows.anchor: أي من هو مستتر بالليل، والليل أستر من النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sārib by day means visible on his route; sarb means a path, as in ‘leave his sarb open.’
rows.anchor: أي من هو ظاهر بالنهار في سربه، يقال: خل له سربه أي طريقه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows equally those who speak aloud and those who conceal their words in themselves.
rows.anchor: والجاهر بنطقه والمضمر في نفسه علم الله فيهم جميعا سواء

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub allows mustakhfin by night to mean visible and sārib by day to mean hidden, as when a wild animal enters its lair.
rows.anchor: وذكر قطرب وجها آخر، ذكر أنه يجوز أن يكون " مستخف بالليل "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression انسرب الوحشي means the wild animal entered its lair.
rows.anchor: يقال: انسرب الوحشي إذا دخل في كناسه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first interpretation is clear and more powerful in depicting God’s knowledge of the unseen.
rows.anchor: والأول بين، وهو أبلغ في وصف علم الغيب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The muʿaqqibāt are angels who succeed one another, each group arriving after the previous one.
rows.anchor: أي للإنسان ملائكة يعتقبون، يأتي بعضهم بعقب بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘They guard him by God’s command’ means they protect him as God commanded, not that they can repel God’s decree.
rows.anchor: المعنى حفظهم إياه من أمر الله، أي مما أمرهم الله تعالى به،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one besides God takes charge of their affairs.
rows.anchor: أي لا يلي أمرهم أحد من دون الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear of rain’s harm concerns the traveler, as in the verse about being harmed by rain.
rows.anchor: خوفا للمسافر، لأن في المطر خوفا على المسافر، كما قال الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hope for rain concerns the resident who benefits from it.
rows.anchor: وطمعا للحاضر لأن تفاعه بالمطر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible reading is fear for anyone harmed by rain and hope for anyone who benefits, since some lands such as Egypt do not benefit from rain.
rows.anchor: خوفا لمن يخاف ضر المطر، لأنه ليس كل بلد ينتفع فيه بالمطر نحو مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavy clouds are laden with water.
rows.anchor: أي التي قد ثقلت بالماء.

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: A tafsīr report identifies thunder as an angel who drives the clouds.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير أنه ملك يزجر السحاب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The thunder’s own sound may be its glorification because it is a great sound; it is singled out for its loudness, alongside the principle that all things glorify God.
rows.anchor: وجائز أن يكون صوت الرعد تسبيحه لأن صوت الرعد من أعظم الأشياء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wāw may be circumstantial: God strikes someone while he disputes about Him; a pre-Islamic man named Irbid asked the Prophet whether their Lord was copper or iron, and a lightning bolt killed him.
rows.anchor: أتى في التفسير أن رجلا من الجاهلية يقال له " اربد "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, after completing the signs of God’s oneness and power to resurrect, the passage turns to their dispute about God.
rows.anchor: لما تمم الله أوصاف ما يدل على توحيده وقدرته على البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shadīd al-miḥāl means mighty in power and punishment; maḥaltuhu means I matched him, and maḥl denotes severity.
rows.anchor: ويقال في اللغة ماحلته محالا، إذا قاويته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those guided to God are those who return to the truth.
rows.anchor: يعني من رجع إلى الحق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alladhīna āmanū is accusative as an appositive to man in the preceding verse: God guides those who believe.
rows.anchor: في موضع نصب ردا على (من)، المعنى يهدي إليه الذين آمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers’ hearts become tranquil when they recall God’s oneness and believe without doubt.
rows.anchor: أي إذا ذكر الله بوحدانيته آمنوا به غير شاكين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alā is a particle of attention and commencement; the tranquil hearts are believers’ hearts, since a disbeliever’s heart is not tranquil.
rows.anchor: ومعنى (ألا بذكر الله تطمئن القلوب) أي التي هي قلوب المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative ḥusnu maʾāb coordinates with ṭūbā; an accusative is also possible, meaning God made good fortune and a good return for them.
rows.anchor: القراءة بالرفع في (وحسن مآب). عطف على (طوبى)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians derive ṭūbā as fuʿlā from ṭayyib, meaning a pleasant life for its recipients.
rows.anchor: عند النحويين فعلى من الطيب. المعنى العيش الطيب لهم.

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet describes ṭūbā as a tree in Paradise.
rows.anchor: وجاء في التفسير عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أن (طوبى) شجرة في الجنة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported gloss says ṭūbā means felicity for them.
rows.anchor: وقيل (طوبى) لهم حسنى لهم،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported gloss says ṭūbā means good for them.
rows.anchor: وقيل طوبى لهم خير لهم.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported view takes ṭūbā as the Indian name of Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقيل (طوبى) لهم اسم الجنة بالهندية.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further gloss reads ṭūbā as a choice or blessing; all these glosses resemble the derivation from ṭayyib.
rows.anchor: وقيل (طوبى) لهم خيرة لهم، وهذا التفسير كله يشبهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response to law is omitted because context supplies it; polytheists had asked for Meccan mountains to be moved aside for estates and gardens and for named people to be revived, and God says this Qur’an could do so.
rows.anchor: ترك جواب " لو " لأن في الكلام دليلا عليه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ signs were proofs of prophethood, such as his hand becoming white and the staff becoming a serpent.
rows.anchor: أي البرهان الذي دل على صحة نبوته، نحو إخراج يده بيضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An akhraja means ‘that he bring out’ or ‘by his bringing out’; an can be lightened or explanatory, as if God told Moses, ‘Bring your people out.’
rows.anchor: ههنا يصلح أن يكون لي معنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parallel about the chiefs going away saying ‘Walk’ means they told their people to walk.
rows.anchor: ومثل هذا: (وانطلق الملأ منهم أن امشوا).

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh allows an with an imperative after ‘I wrote to him’ or ‘I ordered him’; it means reported speech (‘that he should rise’) despite the imperative form.
rows.anchor: قال سيبويه تقول كتبت إليه أن قم، وأمرته أن قم،

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh also allows an to mean ‘that is,’ as in ‘I sent to him: what are you and this?’
rows.anchor: في معنى أي، ومثله أرسلت إليه أن ما أنت وذا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa-dhakkirhum is coordinated with akhrij; remembering God’s days means recalling both His favors and His punishments of Noah’s, ʿĀd’s, and Thamūd’s peoples.
rows.anchor: عطف على (اخرج)، وتذكيرهم بأيام الله، أي تذكيرهم بنعم أيام الله عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following verse about earlier peoples proves that remembrance includes warning from the disasters that befell previous unbelievers.
rows.anchor: والدليل على أن التذكير مشتمل على الإنذار والتحذير مما نزل بمن قبلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘None knows them but God’ means there were later nations whose histories are unknown; genealogists cannot know people who came after those named.
rows.anchor: قد مضى من كان يعلم أنباءها،

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The saying that genealogists are mistaken is reported from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وهذا يروى عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -.

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says the messengers bit their fingertips in anger at what the messengers brought them.
rows.anchor: يروى عن ابن مسعود أنهم عضوا أناملهم غيظا مما أتتهم به الرسل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the people gestured to the messengers to be silent.
rows.anchor: أومأوا إلى الرسل أن اسكتوا.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further interpretation makes the pronouns refer to the messengers: the people rejected their hands, meaning their blessings, through verbal denial.
rows.anchor: الهاء والميم يرجعان على الرسل، المعنى ردوا أيدي الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fī afwāhihim can mean bi-afwāhihim, ‘with their mouths’; both prepositions express the same relation, as in sitting in or by a house.
rows.anchor: ومعنى في أفواههم بأفواههم، أي ردوا تلك النعم بالنطق بالتكذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their statement that they disbelieved what the messengers were sent with is the rejection itself.
rows.anchor: إنا كفرنا بما أرسلتم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sijjīl means clay bearing a written mark, deriving from sijill; the verse about stones of clay marked by God supports this reading.
rows.anchor: من طين عليه كتاب. واشتقاق ذلك من السجل.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One gloss takes al-mutawassimīn as people with discernment or insight.
rows.anchor: قيل المتوسمون المتفرسون،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another gloss takes al-mutawassimīn as people who reflect.
rows.anchor: وقيل المتفكرون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Literally they are observers who examine carefully until recognizing a thing’s true mark; tawassamtu fī fulān means recognizing its sign in him.
rows.anchor: وحقيقته في اللغة المتوسمون النظار المتثبتون في نظرهم حتى يعرفوا حقيقة سمة الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remains of the town lie by a clear, evident road.
rows.anchor: أي لبطريق واضح بين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sign is clear to those who affirm the truth.
rows.anchor: أي لعلامة بينة للمصدقين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of al-Aykah were people of trees; al-ayk means trees, and they lived in a wooded place.
rows.anchor: والأيك الشجر وهؤلا أهل موضع كان ذا شجر.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported account says God punished them for disbelief with days of heat, then their place burst into fire and all perished.
rows.anchor: قيل إنه أخذهم الحر أياما ثم اضطرم عليهم المكان نارا فهلكوا عن آخرهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The combination of inna and the lām is emphatic.
rows.anchor: ومعنى " إن واللام " التوكيد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imām mubīn means a clear road that is followed or intended; the people of al-Ḥijr lived in a valley called al-Ḥijr.
rows.anchor: أي لبطريق يؤتم أي يقصد فيبين، وأصحاب الحجر أصحاب واد يقال له الحجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s responsibility for the straight path means that He makes the road to Him clear through proofs and arguments.
rows.anchor: أي على الله تبيين الطريق المستقيم إليه بالحجج والبراهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jāʾir describes paths that deviate from the truth rather than aim straight toward it.
rows.anchor: جائر أي من السبل طرق غير قاصدة للحق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God wished, He could send a sign that compels everyone to believe; instead He guides whom He wills and calls to a straight path.
rows.anchor: ولكنه عز وجل: يهدي من يشاء ويدعو إلى صراط مستقيم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shajar is the vegetation camels graze, and every plant growing from the earth is called shajar.
rows.anchor: المعنى أنه ينبت الشجر التي ترعاها الإبل،

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet describing horses uses shajar for grazing vegetation: when it is scarce horses are fed meat, which harms them; the text says they are given milk when the land is barren.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر يصف الخيل: نعلفها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tusīmūn means ‘you graze’; the root means letting camels graze, and derives from sīma, a mark, because grazing leaves marks on land.
rows.anchor: أي ترعون، يقال: أسمت الإبل إذا رعيتها، وقد سامت تسوم وهي سائمة إذا رعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular najm and plural nujūm have the same sense, as ‘a dirham’ and ‘dirhams’ can both describe many coins in people’s hands.
rows.anchor: كما تقول: كثر الدرهم في أيدي الناس وكثرت الدراهم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created stars to adorn the lowest heaven, to stone devils, to guide travelers, and to mark years and reckoning.
rows.anchor: النجوم لأشياء منها أنها جعلت زينة للسماء الدنيا، ومنها أنها جعلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading of ‘those you invoke’ varies between second-person plural tadʿūna and third-person plural yudʿawna.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ (تدعون من دون الله) بالتاء والياء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse refers to the idols worshipped by the Arabs: they create nothing and are themselves created.
rows.anchor: يعنى به الأوثان التي كانت تعبدها العرب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols are dead, not alive.
rows.anchor: أي وهم أموات غير أحياء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ayyān means ‘when’; it is accusative with yubʿathūn but indeclinable because it is interrogative, like kam, matā, kayfa, and ayna.
rows.anchor: في موضع نصب بقوله (يبعثون) ولكنه مبني غير منون، لأنه بمعنى الاستفهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final nūn takes fatḥa to resolve two sukūns; after an alif, fatḥa is preferred because it resembles the alif and is lighter.
rows.anchor: قيل الاختيار إذا كان قبل الساكن الأخير ألف أن يفتح،

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh and al-Khalīl say a vocative name such as Asḥār keeps fatḥa when two sukūns meet; similarly, the imperative ghuddu takes fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وزعم سيبويه والخليل أنك إذا رخمت رجلا اسمه أسحار،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One interpretation of wāṣiban is ‘always’: obedience is permanently obligatory.
rows.anchor: قيل معناه دائما، أي طاعة واجبة أبدا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading is that religion and obedience belong to God whether the servant accepts the command or finds it easy; they remain His even when they involve toil, since waṣb is severe fatigue.
rows.anchor: أي له الدين والطاعة، رضي العبد بما يؤمر به أو لم يرض،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about fearing another god appeals to God’s uniqueness as creator and source of every blessing, and His power to destroy unbelievers rather than leave them until repentance.
rows.anchor: أي أفغير الله الذي قد بان لكم أنه وحده، وأنه خالق كل شيء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters’ claim that they worship idols only to bring them nearer to God cannot justify worship of anything besides Him, even when they intend nearness to God alone.
rows.anchor: فأعلم الله - عز وجل - أن لا إله إلا هو، ولا يجوز أن يعبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ‘do not take two gods,’ ithnayn reinforces ilāhayn; likewise wāḥid reinforces the statement that He is one God.
rows.anchor: فذكر اثنين توكيدا لقوله إلهين، كما ذكر الواحد في قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Honey exits through the bee’s mouth, but is attributed to the bellies because food is transformed there; bees move it from belly to mouth, as humans release saliva from the mouth.
rows.anchor: لأن استحالة الأطعمة لا تكون إلا في البطون فيخرج بعضها من الفم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view makes the pronoun in ‘in it is healing’ refer to honey, so the verse says honey heals people.
rows.anchor: قيل إن. الهاء يرجع على العسل، المعنى في العسل شفاء للناس.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view makes the pronoun refer to the Qur’an: its account of bees and other narratives that show God’s oneness heals people.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن الهاء للقرآن، المعنى في القرآن شفاء للناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The honey interpretation is very good; although honey can harm some, water can also kill depending on bodily illness, and many remedies and drinks are based on honey.
rows.anchor: والتفسير في العسل حسن جدا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only the ignorant deny honey’s healing; anyone who understands its benefit, even outside this religious community, acknowledges that honey heals.
rows.anchor: وهذا الاعتراض في أمر العسل إنما هو اعتراض جهلة لا يعرفون قدرة في النفع،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tanzīlan is an accusative verbal noun meaning ‘We sent it down as a sending’; al-ʿulā is the plural of al-ʿulyā, like kubrā and kubar.
rows.anchor: يقال: سماء عليا وسموات على، مثل الكبرى والكبر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative al-Raḥmān is preferred; genitive is also possible as an appositive to man, ‘from the Creator of earth and heavens, the Merciful,’ followed by the statement that He established Himself over the Throne.
rows.anchor: ويجوز الخفض على البدل من " من " المعنى تنزيلا من خالق الأرض والسماوات الرحمن،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though some gloss istawā as ‘took control,’ the linguistic evidence supports the sense conveyed by istawā itself.
rows.anchor: والذي يدل عليه استوى في اللغة على ما فعله من معنى الاستواء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tharā means moisture; what lies beneath the earth is moist, and exegetes likewise gloss ‘beneath the soil’ as what is under the earth.
rows.anchor: الثرى في اللغة الندى، وما تحت الأرض ندى، وجاء في التفسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The secret is what one conceals within oneself; what is more hidden is the unseen known only to God.
rows.anchor: فالسر ما أكننته في نفسك، و " أخفى " ما يكون من الغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yafruṭ means to rush ahead to punish; related forms describe a matter happening early, excess, or falling short, all connected to advancing, since farṭ is one who precedes.
rows.anchor: يقال: قد فرط منه أمر أي قد بدر منه أمر، وقد أفرط في الشيء

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said, ‘I will precede you at the Pond,’ using faraṭ for one who goes ahead.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - " أنا فرطكم على الحوض ".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Peace be on whoever follows guidance’ is not a greeting; it means the follower of guidance is safe from God’s punishment and anger, since this is not an opening encounter.
rows.anchor: ليس يعنى به التحية، وإنما معناه أن من اتبع الهدى سلم من عذاب الله وسخطه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text omits ‘they said to him’ after ‘they went to him’ because context makes it clear; Pharaoh’s next question proves that they spoke to him.
rows.anchor: لأن الكلام قد دل على ذلك فاستغنى عنه أن يقال فيه فأتياه فقالا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created each thing in the form most useful and suitable to it, then guided it to its livelihood.
rows.anchor: معناه خلق كل شيء على الهيئة التي بها ينتفع، والتي هي أصلح الخلق له،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another possible gloss says God guided each creature to the place where its offspring is produced; males instinctively approach females without prior instruction.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل ثم هداه لموضع ما يكون منه الولد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first, broader interpretation is clearer and includes reproductive guidance as part of what benefits each creature.
rows.anchor: والقول الأول ينتظم هذا المعنى، لأنه إذا هداه لمصلحته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses is the one who asks Pharaoh about the earlier generations.
rows.anchor: قال له موسى عليه السلام:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘My Lord does not err or forget’ can mean God does not lose track of the generations or forget them, or that He does not misplace or forget the record.
rows.anchor: معناه لا يضلها ولا ينساها، ولا يضله ربي ولا ينساه، يعنى به الكتاب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍalla has two vowelings; aḍlaltuhu means putting something where its location is unknown, hence causing it to be lost.
rows.anchor: ومعنى ضللت الشيء وضللت بكسر اللام وفتحها أضله وأضله،

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abū Isḥāq says the reading with fatḥa on the yāʾ means ‘He does not stray from my Lord.’
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق من قرأ بالفتح فمعناه لا يضل

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: With ḍamma on the yāʾ, Abū Isḥāq explains that God is not found straying from the record.
rows.anchor: وإذا ضممت الياء فمعناه لا يوجد ربي ضالا عنها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ūlū al-nuhā means people of reason; nuhya is its singular, and reason restrains its possessor from shameful acts and leads to good.
rows.anchor: يقال: فلان ذو نهية ومعناه ذو عقل ينتهي به عن المقابح

rows.speaker: بعض أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Some linguists say a person of nuhya follows the judgment and reason he has reached; the author also considers this sound.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض أهل اللغة: ذو النهية الذي ينتهى إلى رأيه وعقله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun ‘from it’ refers to the earth: God created Adam from soil, continuing the earlier mention of the earth as a cradle with pathways.
rows.anchor: يعنى به الأرض، لأن الله - عز وجل - خلق آدم من تراب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Another time’ attaches to ‘We bring you out’; bringing people out as soil is equivalent to creation, as with Adam.
rows.anchor: متعلق بقوله (منها نخرجكم)، لأن المعنى كمعنى الأول.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forgiven person repents from sin, believes in his Lord, acts obediently, and then remains steadfast in faith.
rows.anchor: أي تاب من ذنبه، وآمن بربه وعمل بطاعته، ثم اهتدى،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aulāʾ is indeclinable with kasra; ʿalā atharī most naturally attaches to it, though it can be a second predicate.
rows.anchor: من صلة (أولاء)، ويجوز أن يكون خبرا بعد خبر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reported form aulāya has no sound basis because yāʾ follows a final alif only in an annexed form such as hudāya; the author knows no famous reader who read it.
rows.anchor: لأن الياء لا تكون بعد الألف آخرة إلا للإضافة نحو هداي،

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ mentioned the form aulāya, which the author rejects.
rows.anchor: وذكرها الفراء، ولا وجه لها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fatannā means God put the people into a trial and tested them.
rows.anchor: أي ألقيناهم في فتنة ومحنة، واختبرناهم.

rows.speaker: بعض أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Some exegetes say the Samaritan was a Copt from Kerman.
rows.anchor: قال بعض أهل التفسير: السامري علج من أهل كرمان

rows.speaker: الأكثر في التفسير
rows.claim: Most exegetical accounts identify him as a prominent Israelite from the tribe of Samira, whose descendants were still known as Samaritans in Syria.
rows.anchor: والأكثر في التفسير أنه كان عظيما من عظماء بني إسرائيل من قبيلة تعرف بالسامرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asaf is intense grief accompanying anger.
rows.anchor: أسف: شديد الحزن مع غضبه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading with kasra in yaḥilli means God’s anger becomes due upon them; ḍamma is also possible, meaning it descends upon them.
rows.anchor: القراءة فيها بالكسر في حاء يحل، على معنى أنه يجب عليكم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mīm of bi-mulkinā may take ḍamma, kasra, or fatḥa: mulk is authority and power, milk is what the hand possesses, and malak is the verbal noun.
rows.anchor: فأصل الملك السلطان والقدرة، والملك ما حوته اليد، والملك المصدر.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation is that they had not failed to keep the appointment because they possessed the right judgment.
rows.anchor: وقيل في بعض التفسير: ما أخلفنا موعدك بأن ملكنا الصواب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible explanation is that they lacked authority or power; they then explain their delay by carrying the people’s ornaments.
rows.anchor: ما أخلفنا موعدك بسلطان كان لنا ولا قدرة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with a doubled, kasra mīm in ḥammalnā means ‘we carried’; the ornaments were gold and silver taken from Pharaoh’s people after the sea cast them ashore.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ (حملنا أوزارا)، بتشديد الميم وكسرها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ornaments are called awzār either as sins or burdens, since sin weighs on its bearer and wizr also means a load; the verse about removing Moses’ burden supports this sense.
rows.anchor: وسميت أوزارا لأن معناهأ الأثام،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They threw the ornaments into the fire, and the Samaritan did the same with ornaments he had.
rows.anchor: فقالوا: حملنا حليا فقذفناها في النار، وكذلك فعل السامري،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One account says the calf mooed like a living bull, prompting people to prostrate when it mooed and rise when it stopped.
rows.anchor: فقيل إنه كان يخور كما يخور الثور من الحيوان، فإذا خار سجدوا له،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another says it made only one moo, supported by the next verse’s statement that it could not return an answer.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: إنما خار خورة واحدة، ودليله:

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the calf’s moo was the whistling of wind entering its hollow interior.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: خواره حفيف الريح إذا دخلت جوفه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Aaron passed by the Samaritan while he was making the calf.
rows.anchor: ويروى أن هارون عليه السلام مر بالسامري وهو يصنع العجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amthaluhum ṭarīqatan describes the person most knowledgeable, in his own estimation, about what he says; ‘you remained only a day’ means exactly that.
rows.anchor: أي أعلمهم عند نفسه بما يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasf is scattering: the mountains are dispersed like scattered dust.
rows.anchor: النسف التذرية تصير الجبال كالهباء المنثور،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qāʿ is a place whose surface is covered by water, and it can also mean good land; ṣafṣaf is level ground.
rows.anchor: القاع من الأرض المكان الذي يعلوه الماء، ويقال المكان الطيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAwaj in a stick or mountain means that it is not level; amt is where one place is thick and another thin.
rows.anchor: العوج في العصا والجبل ألا يكون مستويا، والأمت أن يغلظ مكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no deviation from the caller’s summons: they cannot avoid following him.
rows.anchor: المعنى لا عوج لهم عن دعائه، لا يقدرون أن لا يتبعوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hams is something quiet or hidden; here it means the sound of footsteps.
rows.anchor: والهمس - ههنا - في التفسير صوت وطء الأقدام.
